title: Felix and the Oath
premise: Zephyrine Whitlock has spent her life in the valley of Hollowmere, where an ancient ward keeps magic out — and keeps her beast-speaking gift a secret worth her life. When a dying courier named Felix presses a bloodstained map into her hands and breathes his last, she learns the covenant binding the human realm to the wild lands is failing, and that the Whitlock family's exile was no accident but a sentence. Pursued by the Oathwardens who enforce the old law, Zeph flees the valley with Felix's ghost-bound compass, following the map toward the Sundered Court where the covenant was first sworn. There she discovers the truth: her grandmother broke the oath to save the beasts from enslavement, and only a Whitlock can reforge it — at the cost of surrendering either her gift or her freedom. In the end, Zeph refuses both terms, rewriting the covenant itself so that magic and valley coexist, though the price is her name struck from every record, remembered only by the animals who loved her.
about_author: Silas Joubert is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent fifteen years in remote mountain stations before turning to fiction. Their work blends folkloric fantasy with quiet ecological grief, and 'Felix and the Oath' is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Courier at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A stranger staggers through Hollowmere's boundary stones at dusk, dying of wounds that shouldn't exist where magic cannot follow. With his final breath he presses a map into Zeph's hands and whispers her family name. Emotional beat: dread awakening — the safe world cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Zeph hides the map while burying Felix, lying to the village elders for the first time in her life. Her gift stirs — crows warn of riders on the ridge. She realizes the ward didn't keep Felix's killers out; it kept something in. Beat: guilt braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: POV alternating Zeph and Warden Corvane, the Oathwarden hunting the map. The Wardens reach Hollowmere under pretense of a census, testing villagers' blood for taint. Zeph watches her neighbor fail the test and vanish. Beat: terror made bureaucratic; the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: The Compass That Remembers Him
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The ghost-bound compass begins speaking with fragments of Felix's voice, guiding her past the ward's edge. Crossing the boundary, magic floods back — overwhelming, beautiful, painful. Her first true conversation with a beast beyond the valley nearly kills her. Beat: awe and disorientation.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Following the map through the Ashwood, Zeph finds a burned waystation and a survivor: Tam, a defector Warden who recognizes the map's seal as Whitlock work. Uneasy alliance forms over a fire. Beat: reluctant trust; the enemy gains a human face.

chapters.title: The Sundered Court
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The ruined court where the covenant was sworn hums with broken oaths. Ghost-echoes show Zeph her grandmother standing where she now stands — and refusing something. Corvane ambushes them; Tam is captured covering her escape. Beat: betrayal of hope, cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Grandmother
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A bound spirit — her grandmother's remnant — reveals the truth: the oath demanded beasts as tribute; she shattered it rather than comply, dooming her line to exile. Reforging it demands a Whitlock's sacrifice: gift or freedom. Beat: inheritance reframed as wound, not honor.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. The Warden's own history surfaces — a brother lost to unbound magic, a career built on containing grief. He offers Zeph mercy if she surrenders the map and lets the covenant die, sealing the realms apart forever. Beat: antagonist humanized; temptation sharpened.

chapters.title: The Third Word
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. At the climax, Zeph stands before the covenant stone and speaks neither offered term. Drawing on Felix's compass, her grandmother's refusal, and the gathered beasts, she writes a third word into the oath: kinship. The stone shatters; magic floods the valley. Beat: defiant transcendence.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine (epilogue-flavored). The price of a rewritten covenant: Zeph's name fades from records and memory alike. She returns to Hollowmere unrecognized, living at its edge among animals who still know her. Tam visits, carrying one thing that remembers: Felix's compass, warm in her hand. Beat: bittersweet peace; love outlasting identity.
